fun_facts: The Circle of Fifths was first described by Nikolai Diletskii in the late 1670s
Moving through all 12 keys clockwise visits every note exactly once - like a Hamiltonian path!
The circle can be used to quickly transpose any song to a new key
Jazz musicians often use the circle to create 'ii-V-I' progressions in every key
The pattern of sharps (FCGDAEB) and flats (BEADGCF) are mirror images of each other
Video game composers use the circle to create seamless key changes in adaptive music
The circle is isomorphic to the cyclic group Z₁₂ in abstract algebra
